title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding transforms categorical variables into a set of binary variables. For the 'weather' column, which has three categories ('sunny', 'cloudy', 'rainy'), one-hot encoding will create three new binary columns.

title: Impact of One-Hot Encoding on Model
text: When you add all one-hot encoded features to a model, it can lead to multicollinearity if the original categorical variable is not removed. This is because the sum of the one-hot encoded columns will always equal one, introducing perfect multicollinearity.

title: Understanding Multicollinearity
text: Multicollinearity occurs when two or more predictors in a regression model are correlated, meaning that one can be linearly predicted from the others with a substantial degree of accuracy. This can cause issues in estimating the coefficients of the model.
